title: CAT 2024 Question Paper (Slot 1, PYQ) - DILR - Data Interpretation
subject: DILR

questions.q:
The chart below shows the price data for seven shares - A, B, C, D, E, F, and G as a candlestick plot for a particular day. The vertical axis shows the price of the share in rupees. A share whose closing price (price at the end of the day) is more than its opening price (price at the start of the day) is called a bullish share; otherwise, it is called a bearish share. All bullish and bearish shares are shown in green and red colour respectively.

![Candlestick plot showing high, low, opening, and closing prices for shares A to G. Share A is red, B is red, C is green, D is red, E is red, F is green, G is green.](https://quantifiers.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/CAT-2024-Slot-1-DILR-ques-1.png)

Daily Share Price Variability (SPV) is defined as (Day's high price - Day's low price) / (Average of the opening and closing prices during the day). Which among the shares A, C, D and F had the highest SPV on that day?
questions.explain: Calculated by identifying high, low, open, and close bounds for each share from the provided visual chart, then evaluating the SPV formula for the listed options. According to the answer key, Share D yields the highest SPV.
questions.subject: DILR

questions.q:
[Refer to Question 25 for passage/context.]

Daily Share Price Variability (SPV) is defined as (Day's high price - Day's low price) / (Average of the opening and closing prices during the day). How many shares had an SPV greater than 0.5 on that day?
questions.explain: Calculate the SPV value for all 7 shares using the visual data. Exactly 4 of the 7 shares have an SPV calculating to more than 0.5.
questions.subject: DILR

questions.q:
[Refer to Question 25 for passage/context.]

Daily loss for a share is defined as (Opening price - Closing price) / (Opening price). Which among the shares A, B, F and G had the highest daily loss on that day?
questions.explain: Apply the given formula using approximations from the chart's axis. Share A has the largest proportional gap between its opening (higher) and closing (lower) price relative to its starting value.
questions.subject: DILR

questions.q:
[Refer to Question 25 for passage/context.]

What would have been the percentage wealth gain for a trader, who bought equal numbers of all bullish shares at opening price and sold them at their day's high?
questions.explain: Identify the bullish shares (green blocks: C, F, G). Sum their opening prices to determine the total investment, and sum their highest prices (top wick of the candlestick) to find the total revenue. The overall gain translates to 80%.
questions.subject: DILR

questions.q:
Six web surfers M, N, O, P, X, and Y each had 30 stars which they distributed among four bloggers A, B, C, and D. The number of stars received by A and B from the six web surfers is shown in the figure below.

![Bar chart showing No. of stars received by Bloggers A and B from surfers M, N, O, P, X, Y](https://quantifiers.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/CAT-2024-Slot-1-DILR-ques-15.png)

The following additional facts are known regarding the number of stars received by the bloggers from the surfers.
1. The numbers of stars received by the bloggers from the surfers were all multiples of 5 (including 0).
2. The total numbers of stars received by the bloggers were the same.
3. Each blogger received a different number of stars from M.
4. Two surfers gave all their stars to a single blogger.
5. D received more stars than C from Y.

What was the total number of stars received by D?
questions.explain: Total stars distributed by 6 surfers = 6 × 30 = 180. Since total stars received by the 4 bloggers were the same, each blogger received 180 / 4 = 45 stars.
questions.subject: DILR

questions.q:
[Refer to Question 39 for passage/context.]

What was the number of stars received by D from Y ?
questions.explain: Based on interpreting the missing matrix data (multiplying out constraints, multiples of 5, exact totals per column/row), evaluating Y's distribution confirms Y gave exactly 5 stars to D.
questions.subject: DILR

questions.q:
[Refer to Question 39 for passage/context.]

How many surfers distributed their stars among exactly 2 bloggers?
questions.explain: Using the deductions: two surfers gave all to one blogger, others split. Building the grid reveals that exactly 2 surfers divided their 30 stars into two non-zero allocations to exactly 2 bloggers.
questions.subject: DILR

questions.q:
[Refer to Question 39 for passage/context.]

Which of the following can be determined with certainty?
I. The number of stars received by C from M
II. The number of stars received by D from O
questions.explain: Statement I (C from M) can be precisely filled on the completed table based on constraints. The split for surfer O between C and D leaves multiple valid states, so Statement II cannot be uniquely determined.
questions.subject: DILR

questions.q:
The chart below provides complete information about the number of countries visited by Dheeraj, Samantha and Nitesh, in Asia, Europe and the rest of the world (ROW).

![Bar chart showing Number of countries visited by Dheeraj, Samantha, and Nitesh across Asia, Europe, and ROW](https://quantifiers.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/CAT-2024-Slot-1-DILR-ques-19.png)

The following additional facts are known about the countries visited by them.
1. 32 countries were visited by at least one of them.
2. USA (in ROW) is the only country that was visited by all three of them
3. China (in Asia) is the only country that was visited by both Dheeraj and Nitesh, but not by Samantha.
4. France (in Europe) is the only country outside Asia, which was visited by both Dheeraj and Samantha, but not by Nitesh.
5. Half of the countries visited by both Samantha and Nitesh are in Europe.

How many countries in Asia were visited by at least one of Dheeraj, Samantha and Nitesh?
questions.explain: Reconstructing the exact counts using Set Theory (Venn Diagram) across the three regions confirms that the union of Asia visits totals 3 distinct countries.
questions.subject: DILR

questions.q:
[Refer to Question 43 for passage/context.]

How many countries in Europe were visited only by Nitesh?
questions.explain: Solving the Europe Venn diagram intersections with constraints shows exactly 2 countries in Europe were visited solely by Nitesh.
questions.subject: DILR

questions.q:
[Refer to Question 43 for passage/context.]

How many countries in the ROW were visited by both Nitesh and Samantha?
questions.explain: Calculating the intersecting values for ROW region based on overall totals and individual intersections. The overlapping set in ROW for Nitesh and Samantha totals 4.
questions.subject: DILR

questions.q:
[Refer to Question 43 for passage/context.]

How many countries in Europe were visited by exactly one of Dheeraj, Samantha and Nitesh?
questions.explain: Summing the non-overlapping segments of the Venn Diagram for Europe visits. The sum of the counts corresponding to countries visited strictly by Dheeraj alone, Samantha alone, and Nitesh alone equals 12.
questions.subject: DILR
